title: Compact-support projection formula at all coefficient stages
statement:
In the six-functor datum of
[def-fix-six-functor-datum], let $f:X\to Y$ be
separated of finite
type, let $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and
$L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, using the
finite-Tor subcategory.
The
projection transformation, built from the
derived tensor and pullback
and the finite-level compact-support direct image of
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] and its higher-coefficient versions
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support],
is then an isomorphism at every coefficient stage:

$$
\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}:Rf_!K\otimes^L_{\Lambda}L
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf_!\bigl(K\otimes^L_{\Lambda}Lf^*L\bigr),
$$

natural in $K$ and $L$, compatible with the composition law of
[thm-sf-comp-composition] (associativity pentagon), with the compactification comparisons, with
finite reduction on the stated finite-Tor domains and scalar extension,
and with the identification
$Rf_!\cong Rf_*$ for proper $f$. At the rational and algebraically closed stages, when $X=X_0\otimes_{k_0}k$, $Y=Y_0\otimes_{k_0}k$ for separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes and $f$ is the geometric base change of a separated finite-type $k_0$-morphism $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$, the isomorphism restricts to the Weil categories [def-wf-weil-category], with tensor as in [def-wf-tensor-product]. A projection formula for the
derived direct image is asserted
only in the proper case, where it is this same statement via
$Rf_!\cong Rf_*$.

proof.text: Use the operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum] and fix the projection transformation of [def-exchange-projection]. For a compactification $f=pj$, its component is the projection map of $Rp_*$ at $(j_!K,L)$ followed by $Rp_*$ of $j_!K\otimes^LLp^*L\cong j_!(K\otimes^LLf^*L)$. At finite coefficients $Rf_!^c=Rp_*j_!$ is [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]; at the integral, rational and algebraically closed stages use precisely the completed, localized and common-stage functors of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Thus throughout the proof PF means this specified natural transformation, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism with the same endpoints.

source.place: Proof, first sentence; statement, projection transformation and coefficient stages

proof.text: Let $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], choose bounded constructible etale representatives $K_0,L_0$ with witnesses $\nu_X^*K_0\cong K$, $\nu_Y^*L_0\cong L$. The converse direction of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] transfers the finite Tor interval of $L$ to $L_0$; $L_0$ is bounded below because it is bounded. Now [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula] applies to $f,K_0,L_0$ and its witnessed pro-etale realizations. It says exactly that the component of the transformation in step 1 is invertible and natural in $K,L$. No finite Tor condition on $K$ is needed here.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: finite coefficient formula, with intrinsic pro-etale objects supplied witnesses

proof.text: For $1\le m\le n$, assume $K,L$ are in the finite-Tor domains and write $\rho_T(-)=-\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}$ on each scheme. For the tensor input, [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] preserves the Tor interval of $L$, and [lem-sf-tensor-ctf](ii) gives finite Tor amplitude for $K\otimes^LLf^*L$ by adding the two intervals. Thus the compact-support coefficient comparison applies to this input as well as to $K$. The coefficient comparison of [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change] is an isomorphism for the compact-support direct image, and [lem-fix-operation-reduction] gives the tensor and pullback comparisons together with preservation of the units and counits used in the mate defining [def-exchange-projection]. Define the comparison $u$ on the source of PF by first applying the tensor comparison and then the compact-support comparison to $K$, and define $v$ on its target by applying the compact-support comparison to $K\otimes^LLf^*L$ and then the tensor and pullback comparisons. Expanding the two composites through a compactification $f=pj$, the proper factor is the transpose of the same counit composite (the counit identity in [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]), while the open factor is the same extension-by-zero tensor map after coefficient change. Hence $v\circ\rho(\operatorname{PF}_{n})=\operatorname{PF}_{m}\circ u$. This is an equality of the specified mate composites, so it does not use an axiom asserting that PF is invertible. The finite formula [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula] supplies invertibility at both levels.

Work integrally with the actual projection component $u:S\to T$ specified in step 1, not a lift chosen from its reductions. The objects $K,L$ are derived complete and have uniformly bounded constructible reductions by [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. By [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] their reductions have uniform finite Tor intervals. By [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible], $Lf^*L$, $K\widehat\otimes^LLf^*L$, and $S=(Rf_!K)\widehat\otimes^LL$ are integral constructible; here [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible] first supplies $Rf_!K$ and also supplies $T=Rf_!(K\widehat\otimes^LLf^*L)$. Thus both endpoints of $u$ are derived complete. Apply the integral clause of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]: its comparisons identify $S_n,T_n$ with the finite projection endpoints, and its preservation of units, counits and tensor comparisons identifies the reduction of the actual composite $u$ with $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_n,L_n}$. That finite map is invertible by [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]. The cone of $u$ remains in the complete constructible category by [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated] (rotate its cone triangle to use the stated extension closure). Its first reduction is zero. The isomorphism-detection clause of [sk-lem-pe-derived-nakayama] therefore proves $u$ invertible. This proves invertibility of the specified map itself and its reduction square; it does not construct a map from an incoherent family, or deduce equality of maps from conservativity.

source.place: Integral reconstruction sentence: concrete reduction of the canonical map and derived Nakayama

proof.text: The raw localization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] has the same objects as the integral category, so choose integral representatives of the two rational inputs. The rational operations and transformations are the localized integral ones by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] and [def-exchange-projection]. Apply localization to the map and its inverse from step 4. For an extension of finite coefficient fields use the scalar-comparison clause of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]: it commutes with the operations and preserves the units, counits and tensor associators defining PF, so it identifies extension of this very component with the component over the larger field. Exactness of the extension functor is [lem-weil-scalar-extension-exact-triangulated]; preservation of an inverse also follows simply from functoriality. For algebraically closed coefficients choose one common finite field for both inputs and the map, as in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. The supplied comparisons in [def-exchange-projection] satisfy the identity and tower cocycle. Hence enlarging the field gives the same morphism class, and the finite-stage inverse gives its inverse class. This proves the field formulas and their scalar compatibility without an axiomatized projection theorem.

source.place: Field-passage sentence: localization and canonical scalar comparisons

proof.text: For finite coefficients, [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] gives an étale-origin witness for every bounded constructible pro-étale input, and [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] transfers the finite-Tor interval to the étale representative. The finite projection lemma [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula] explicitly includes the pro-étale realizations with these witnesses, so it gives invertibility of the actual pro-étale PF component, including arbitrary finite-level $K$ and finite-Tor $L$. At the integral stage, the pro-étale operations and their reduction maps are the ones in the tower definition [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], and step 4 identifies their inverse-limit map with PF. Rationalization and common-stage scalar extension then give the field stages by step 5. Thus no abstract pro-étale projection axiom or replacement of the completed coefficient system by a discrete étale one is used.

We establish the finite coherence identities before imposing constructibility. Write $P_u=Lu^*$, $R_u=Ru_*$ and $\pi_u$ for the counit-defined map of [def-exchange-projection]. Under the adjunction-normalized direct-image compositor [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition], the identity to prove for composable $u,v$ is $\pi_{vu;M,N}=R_v(\pi_{u;M,P_vN})\,\pi_{v;R_uM,N}$, with the pullback and tensor identifications inserted. Transpose both sides under $P_uP_v\dashv R_vR_u$. By [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] its counit is $\varepsilon_u\circ P_u\varepsilon_vR_u$. Both transposes are therefore the composite from $P_uP_v(R_vR_uM\otimes N)$ to $M\otimes P_uP_vN$ which first distributes the two pullbacks over tensor, then applies $P_u\varepsilon_{v,R_uM}$ to the first factor, and finally $\varepsilon_{u,M}$ to that factor. Naturality of the tensor-pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] moves the middle counit across that comparison. The two iterated tensor comparisons agree: on flat-term K-flat models [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] both send a local pure tensor to the same pure tensor, and their total-complex differentials have the same signs. The adjunction bijection now gives the equality. The same calculation with an identity adjunction gives the identity constraint. Iterating this fixed counit composite proves equality of all parenthesizations. These identities require no Tor hypothesis on $M$ and no invertibility of $\pi_u$.

At a finite coefficient level, the normalized proper/open comparison in any commutative proper/open square satisfies the projection identity of [lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate]. Its clopen-projection normalization includes non-Cartesian refinement squares. The same cited statement gives this identity for intrinsic semilinear-system maps before evaluation; [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] identifies their finite evaluations with the canonical finite maps. No Tor or boundedness hypothesis is used in this local mate identity.

For a refinement $u:c_1\to c_2$, use precisely $\theta_u=R_{p_2}(\gamma_u^{-1})c_{p_2,u}$ of [def-sf-refinement-comparison-isomorphism]. Step 7 makes the direct-image compositor commute with projection. Step 8, applied to $r=\mathrm{id}_X$, $k=j_1$, $i=j_2$, $p=u$, makes $\gamma_u$ and its inverse commute with the open tensor/projection maps. Substitute these two identities in the defining composite of $\theta_u$; they give
$$\theta_{u,K\otimes Lf^*L}\operatorname{PF}^{c_1}_{f,K,L}
=\operatorname{PF}^{c_2}_{f,K,L}(\theta_{u,K}\otimes1).$$
The comparison cocycle and common refinements of [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] extend this equality to arbitrary compactifications. Its witnessed domain applies: [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] gives bounded constructible finite-Tor $Lf^*L$, and [lem-sf-tensor-ctf](i), with that as the finite-Tor factor and the symmetry of tensor, gives bounded constructibility of $K\otimes^LLf^*L$ even for arbitrary bounded constructible $K$. [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] gives witnesses for $K$ and for the bounded constructible tensor appearing in the finite formula [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]. No finite Tor assumption on $K$ was used in either local identity. Hence the specified finite PF descends independently of compactification on the full domain of the item.

source.place: Tags 0F7B and 0F7G: refinement normalization and tensor compatibility

proof.text: For composable $f,g$ between finite-type $k$-schemes, all schemes are Noetherian and qcqs: apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] over the spectrum of the field, then [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Choose a compactification $Y\xhookrightarrow{i}\overline Y\xrightarrow{s}Z$ of $g$ and use [lem-weil-pbc-compatible-compactification-triangle] to obtain $X\xhookrightarrow{j}V\xhookrightarrow{b}\overline X$ with $q:V\to Y$, $p:\overline X\to\overline Y$ proper, $f=qj$ and $pb=iq$ cartesian; the compactification schemes are again of finite type over the field. Its normalized comparison $\alpha_{g,f}$ is that of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] and, at finite pro-etale level, of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]; under the counit-normalized direct-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], the open comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] and open composition [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition] it is the canonical compositor of [thm-sf-comp-composition]. The finite-level counit-mate calculation [lem-sf-composition-projection-mate] gives the displayed equation relating $\alpha_{g,f}$ and the three specified projection maps for arbitrary $K,L$, and gives the same equality of actual semilinear-system maps before evaluation. The associative compositor in [thm-sf-comp-composition] then identifies all three-fold parenthesizations.

Use the coherent system operations and realization isomorphisms $c_V$ of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. The proper/open and composition projection identities hold as actual system equalities by [lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate] and [lem-sf-composition-projection-mate]; the counit calculation of step 7 applies in these same ringed diagram categories. Their refinement consequence is the substitution of step 9. For the integral inputs, step 4 supplies the common Tor and constructibility bounds required for every intermediate expression in $c_V$. Apply the total-limit functor and the canonical direct-image comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits], with $A=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(\varpi_E)$; its finite perfect quotients are the usual two-term DVR resolutions. The $c_V$ isomorphisms intertwine units, counits, tensor, composition and proper/open maps, including nested compact support. Conjugating the system equalities by $c_V$ therefore gives the asserted integral equations for the specified maps. The coefficient comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] and the localized/common-stage functors of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] preserve these equations at the field stages. No equality is inferred from finite evaluation or from conservativity.

source.place: Integral coherence sentence, repaired concrete step 11

proof.text: If $f$ is proper, choose the compactification with $j=\operatorname{id}$ and $p=f$ in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] and [def-exchange-projection]. By the defining proper-coincidence identification in [def-fix-six-functor-datum] (equivalently the finite compact-support definition), $Rf_!$ is $Rf_*$. The projection component is then exactly the direct-image projection mate for $p$. Its invertibility follows by applying the finite, integral-tower, and scalar-extension arguments of steps 2--5 to this proper morphism; no direct-image projection formula is asserted for a nonproper morphism.

For finite-type geometric fibres $W\in\{X,Y\}$ of a fixed finite-field model, a finite affine cover of $W$ has finitely generated $k$-algebras as coordinate rings, which are Noetherian by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]; with [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] this verifies the Noetherian finite-dimensional hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], and $\ell\ne p$ is invertible on $W$. That theorem identifies the integral constructible category used by [def-wf-weil-category] with the completed category in the six-functor conventions. The canonical ordinary/completed tensor comparison and its completion unit are supplied by [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion] and [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. The technical Frobenius-compatibility of this comparison is exactly [lem-wf-tensor-completion-frobenius], while [def-wf-tensor-product] defines the target tensor map. The preservation nodes [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] and [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible] keep all operation outputs in these domains. Thus the six-functor tensor is canonically identified with the Weil tensor, compatibly with Frobenius, before applying the equivariance result in step 14.

source.place: Item proof step 13, canonical tensor model and Frobenius compatibility

proof.text: For the Weil assertion impose the finite-field model stated in the corrected statement, and let the inputs carry Weil structures. At $E$-coefficients choose integral representatives of the underlying objects only, to apply the preservation assertions of step 13; the Weil isomorphisms remain morphisms in the rational category. No integral lift of a Weil isomorphism is required. At $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ choose a common finite coefficient field for the two Weil objects, as in [def-wf-weil-category]. The preceding step verifies that the pullback, tensor and compact-support functors have bounded constructible outputs in precisely these coefficient categories. Now [lem-fix-weil-operations] applies to $f_0$ and its geometric fiber $f$: these underlying operations carry their canonical Weil structures and the specified projection transformation is equivariant. Read the tensor Frobenius via [def-wf-tensor-product] and the canonical tensor identification of step 13. Thus, at that finite coefficient field, the underlying projection isomorphism is a morphism between the required Weil objects. The finite-field model is needed for this Weil assertion; the preceding non-Weil projection formula retains its separated finite-type hypotheses.

source.place: Weil-equivariance sentence, after checking coefficient models and constructible domains

proof.text: At the finite coefficient field just chosen, write $u:S\to T$ for the projection component and $\varphi_S,\varphi_T$ for its Weil maps. Step 5 makes $u$ invertible there, and step 14 gives $u\varphi_S=\varphi_T\Phi^*(u)$. Multiply on the left by $u^{-1}$ and on the right by $\Phi^*(u^{-1})$ to obtain $\varphi_S\Phi^*(u^{-1})=u^{-1}\varphi_T$. Thus the inverse is a commuting Weil morphism by [def-wf-weil-category], so $u$ is an isomorphism in the finite-stage Weil category. For algebraically closed coefficients take the class of this inverse at the common finite stage; the definition's composition rule makes its two composites the identity classes. This proves invertibility in the common-stage Weil category itself. The underlying naturality equations are equations of Weil morphisms, so they also prove the asserted naturality after this restriction.

source.place: Weil-equivariance sentence, inverse calculation at a common finite coefficient field

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q47-789250d08 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 15 steps and the three new nodes in full; reviewed all four changed steps against their cited statements and the other eleven against Q41's reviewed split; and checked Stacks 0F7B, which uses a commutative, not necessarily Cartesian, square. All three new statements are true and strictly smaller than the item. (1) lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate: s=(k,r) is open and proper, hence clopen; transposing under P_p⊣R_p reduces the identity to α (β followed by π_s) commuting with the open tensor isomorphisms, which can be checked after s^*. (2) lem-sf-composition-projection-mate: s∘p∘b∘j=g∘f, γ is invertible because b(V) lies over Y, and non-separated schemes are needed because def-fix-six-functor-datum allows them. (3) lem-wf-tensor-completion-frobenius: follows from χ being natural and compatible with Φ^*. Edge cases checked: identity maps, a Cartesian square, a refinement with an extra disjoint proper component, f=id, and the unit tensor. Not duplicates of lem-pur-system-level-projection-formula-coherence (requires separated schemes), prop-sf-pf-coherence (abstract datum), lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus (defines γ but has no projection maps) or def-wf-automorphism-completed-transport. No cycle; no SGA citation. Three faults fixed in fixes/: (a) E1/C1: step 10 had dropped the existence of the compatible compactification triangle (lem-weil-pbc-compatible-compactification-triangle) and its Noetherian/qcqs hypotheses (lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian, lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated), plus lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison; restored.
